operations.name: Joseph Kuzma

expected.charges: Conspiracy to advocate overthrow of the government (Smith Act)
expected.sentence:
One of the Philadelphia Nine, a Communist Party functionary tied to Philadelphia-area labor organizing. Arrested in the 1953 raids and indicted for Smith Act conspiracy; convicted in 1954. In 1957 the Third Circuit reversed the conviction and ordered a new trial for Kuzma and several co-defendants.

Verdict as recorded: Convicted in 1954; conviction reversed on appeal (1957) with a new trial ordered

operations.source: Primary United States v Kuzma141F.Supp91 February11,1954 opinion dates indictment August17,1953 and identifies UnitedStatesAttorney W.WilsonWhite: https://www.leagle.com/decision/1954232141fsupp911210 . expected.description: Bobby Masao Nagahara was a Japanese American participant in the Heart Mountain draft-resistance movement. After being confined at Heart Mountain during World War II, he was prosecuted for refusing military conscription and imprisoned at McNeil Island in Washington.

Camp incarceration not substituted for criminal-prison admission.
